items.title: Edward "Eddie" Richardson Interview, 1960-10-29
items.q: One of the trumpet players I know over there are Charlie Love and Peter Bocash that I can think of offhand, Old Man Allen and Sonny Allen.

ctx.x: Everybody be agreeable. Just a second. We're talking about the dance halls and lawn parties and all that, you said you heard Sun Allen and Celestan. That's right. And what about lawn parties? Do you remember who played those? Well Buddy P.T. and Sam, they played those lawn parties. And there's another musician, I'm trying to call his name. No I can't think of his name now. A trumpet player too. Who was Sam? You said Sam played him. Sam Morgan. Yeah, that was a trumpet player too. That was Albert Morgan's brother.…
Well about how often were you playing parades?

items.title: Edward "Eddie" Richardson Interview, 1960-10-29
items.q: I can remember in those halls they'd have sometime, this fella from over the river, trumpet player, Sun Allen. He'd be over there in those halls sometime.

ctx.x: Dick Allen. I see. Where were you born, Richardson? In New Orleans. What section? They call it the battlefield. That's over around Lafayette and Cypress. Lafayette and Cypress. Yeah. You know I forgot to put today's date on this thing and what are we doing on it? See we're recording in the library in Seminar Room 2, Tulane University. And what's today's date? October the, I can't think. 29th I believe. October the 29th, 1960. So you were born around Cypress and Lafayette, that's your neighborhood? That's right.…
